summary: Route finite resource payloads and retirement through the host executor boundary

replay.detail: Native membership and execution-root journals remain authoritative; no replay or durable byte changes.

schema.detail: Typed commands are internal; no wire, claim or journal schema changes.

rules.detail: Graph planning retains program/shell decisions. Resource commands retain attempt, owner, cancellation and exact-generation fences at physical payload release and retirement.

compatibility.detail: Existing native resource admission and recovery semantics remain unchanged. Accepted signals remain distinct from positive retirement evidence.

downtime.detail: No topology cutover or migration is performed.

manual.detail: No configuration change or operator action is required.

recovery.detail: The planner establishes the existing durable authority before recovery. Physical mutation and asynchronous retirement completion invalidate retained host observations before waking graph adoption.
